meta.niche: Cloud monitoring, observability, and application performance management (APM) software

analysis.summary: Rivals are pushing AI agent observability. New Relic publishes the most, and Sumo Logic targets Datadog buyers directly, while Datadog shows no new or updated pages in 30 days.

points.text: New Relic published 23 new pages in 30 days, mostly opinion and launches on AI and autonomous operations (software that fixes issues with less human input).
Sumo Logic updated five comparison pages, including Datadog vs. Sumo Logic, which suggests it is going after buyers weighing a switch.
Datadog, Dynatrace and Splunk show no new or updated pages in 30 days. Grafana Labs added 10 and Elastic added 17.

Datadog.play: No new or updated pages in 30 days across 3158 pages. No page-level detail in the data.

New Relic.play: 23 new pages: AI and autonomous operations opinion, AI product launches, and best-tool lists.

Dynatrace.play: No new articles. One bulk change on 2026-10-19: 38 pages edited, 31 launched together.

Splunk.play: No new or updated pages in 30 days. All 1810 pages sit under one /en_us/ section.

Grafana Labs.play: 10 new pages: feature launches, release notes, and how-tos for Grafana Cloud and OpenTelemetry.

Elastic Observability.play: 17 new pages, mostly releases, partner news, and security and AI items. Little observability content.
Elastic Observability.aimed: Existing customers, public sector, enterprise buyers

Sumo Logic.play: Refreshed 12 pages: head-to-head SIEM comparisons, landing pages, and AI security and observability pages.
Sumo Logic.aimed: Buyers comparing security and log tools

shared.title: AI agent observability
shared.text: New Relic has launches and a how-to, Grafana has agent SLOs, Elastic has LLM checking, Sumo has an AI page. AI is the main theme to answer.

shared.title: Yearly research reports
shared.text: New Relic's 2026 Observability Forecast, Grafana's 5th annual survey and Elastic's Total Economic Impact study. Each builds a citable proof point for buyers.

shared.title: Comparison pages
shared.text: New Relic posts 'best tools' and alternatives lists. Sumo Logic posts head-to-head pages, one naming Datadog. Both aim at people choosing a vendor.

gaps.title: Datadog-owned comparisons
gaps.text: Sumo Logic writes the Datadog vs. Sumo page itself. Datadog can publish its own fair, up-to-date versions against Sumo, New Relic and Grafana.

gaps.title: AI agent how-tos
gaps.text: Only New Relic (SRE agent) and Grafana (agent SLOs) have one how-to each. Step-by-step guides for running agents in production are open.

gaps.title: Observability cost control guides
gaps.text: Only Grafana (Adaptive Metrics) and one New Relic FinOps list touch spend. Practical guides on cutting data costs are thinly covered.

versus.New Relic: Publishes far more, with heavy AI opinion and launches, and category lists. Datadog's 30-day output is zero, and its page types are not shown.
versus.Dynatrace: Both show no new articles in 30 days. Dynatrace made one bulk edit and launch on 2026-10-19, which is a site change, not content.
versus.Splunk: Both are quiet, with no new or updated pages in 30 days. Splunk's site is one /en_us/ section, and neither has page detail.
versus.Grafana Labs: Grafana ships steady feature and how-to posts, 10 new in 30 days, on a huge docs-led site. Datadog added none.
versus.Elastic Observability: Elastic posted 17 new pages, mostly release notes, partners and security news. Datadog posted none, but Elastic's observability depth looks thin.
versus.Sumo Logic: Sumo refreshed 12 pages and names Datadog in a direct comparison. Datadog had no updates, so Sumo is shaping that buyer story.
